open_questions.question: Why is retail QL achievement in Delhi stuck at 34% despite pipeline discussions every week?
Why is Ahmedabad business not shaping up despite above-market salary, most aggressive incentives, and Neerav's experience? What is the root cause?
When will insurance data tracking be consistently delivered daily (waterfall, issued, pipeline, login, lead stage)?
What is the correct model for E2E business sourced by one city but fulfilled by another - how should it be attributed in reporting?
How does Ambak compound beyond the 2026 AOP targets - when do strategic accounts and builder relationships become the dominant revenue driver?
Will the institutional and E2E joint first-of-month review (decided yesterday) actually happen with a format and owner?

risks: Retail QL collapse in Delhi (34%) will create a June disbursement gap - no clear recovery plan.
Ahmedabad has no ABM after multiple review cycles; October AOP assumes 85 CR from a city that has not consistently crossed 20 CR.
Training scheduling gaps (12-day programs stretching to 16+ days) directly impair RM ramp time when 26% monthly growth requires rapid onboarding.
Out-of-system E2E cases (~20 CR) are creating visibility blackouts; Rashi and Vijay cannot reconcile numbers without manual case reviews.
MAHADA 2600 leads arriving first week of June risk being absorbed into the general pipeline and under-executed without a dedicated campaign structure.
26% monthly growth targets May-August are extremely aggressive given Delhi stagnation, Ahmedabad underperformance, and Bangalore not yet scaled.
Insurance visibility was absent before investor meeting at 2 PM - if insurance is material to May P&L story, this is a significant gap.
meeting_dynamics: Raghu carried all critical probing for 80+ minutes; functional leads and city heads were reactive, not proactive - third straight meeting with this pattern.
E2E pipeline reconciliation consumed 30+ minutes without in-room resolution; 76 CR target should not require a manual case-by-case review 2 weeks before month end.

Raghu's direct critique of Ankit ('efforts are kam, understanding is weak') was unusually personal and specific; Ankit's response pattern (partial acknowledgment + reference to ongoing actions) was mild deflection.
Neerav gave consistent reassurance on Ahmedabad without structural solutions; ABM hiring has been discussed for multiple cycles with no post-mortem on why it has not closed.
Insurance was visibly unready - Tarun and Hitesh were not added to the call; no one owned this preparation failure.
MAHADA 2600 leads received fewer than 5 minutes of discussion despite Raghu flagging it as an insanely large opportunity; bandwidth concerns were raised without escalation or resolution.
